items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: A fellow by the name of Freeman Mitchell was booking bands... And he paid us well.

ctx.x: About what year was that? That was long about 1921.

Yeah, about 21, maybe about 1920. Anyway, we all got this band and we got lots of work. We just got to clean up right now. A fellow by the name of Freeman Mitchell was booking bands. He had a little capital because he worked at the roundhouse for the S.P. Railroad Company. He had a little money to invest and he was lucky with it. And he paid us well. We opened up the Arts Brothers Temple. We opened up the Pilgrim Hall and played there. We got to be, I'll tell you how popular we were. We got so popular that Duke…

When the red light would go on, then you start to record it. Now the man in the back that's recording it, there was a little light thread would come off of that disc and it would pile up and then you'd have to wrap it up and take it off and throw it on the floor. And that was one continuous operation until you cut the disc. And then the lights would go on and nobody said a word, nothing dropped on the floor, you couldn't breathe too hard. That's right. Today it's a lot different.
